Gasification of municipal solid waste and refuse-derived fuel: A critical multiscale review of challenges, contradictions, and scalability pathways
abstract: Municipal solid waste (MSW) and refuse-derived fuel (RDF) continue to accumulate at unsustainable rates, yet conventional disposal routes are increasingly constrained by regulatory, environmental, and land-use pressures. Gasification has been positioned as a versatile waste-to-energy technology capable of converting heterogeneous carbonaceous streams into syngas while supporting resource recovery and decarbonization. However, a critical examination of the literature reveals that reported advantages in syngas yield, tar reduction, energy efficiency, and environmental performance are predominantly derived from idealized or pre-processed feedstocks under controlled laboratory or pilot conditions, masking fundamental contradictions that emerge at the commercial scale. This review provides a critical multiscale assessment of MSW/RDF gasification, integrating feedstock heterogeneity, reactor configurations (fixed-bed, fluidized-bed, entrained-flow, rotary-kiln, and plasma), operational parameters, catalytic strategies, and downstream syngas utilization. Comparative analysis of performance metrics exposes non-monotonic trends in cold gas efficiency, carbon conversion, and tar formation driven by real-world variability in moisture, chlorine, sulfur, and alkali content. Catalyst deactivation mechanisms, reactor-specific trade-offs, and the limitations of current life cycle and techno-economic assessments are shown to undermine claims of superiority over incineration. Persistent gaps in standardization, long-term stability data, and holistic sustainability accounting are identified as primary barriers to scalability. By foregrounding these contradictions rather than incremental optimizations, the analysis delineates the conditions under which gasification can transition from a transitional technology to a genuinely transformative platform for circular waste valorization and negative-emission pathways. Targeted advances in real-feedstock validation, hybrid reactor design, digital process control, and policy-aligned demonstration are required to close the gap between laboratory promise and industrial viability.

Hydrogen evolution catalysis over metal carbides with Pt-like electronic structure
abstract: Water electrolysis offers a sustainable route to hydrogen production, but its practical viability hinges on the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), which is kinetically constrained by a high activation barrier. Metal carbides such as Mo 2 C and WC, featuring Pt-like d -band electronic structures, have attracted interest as low-cost HER catalysts, yet a framework linking their electronic configuration to catalytic performance is absent. This review fills this gap by systematically exploring d -band modulation through defect engineering, nonmetal incorporation, and metal doping. We establish how each strategy alters the d -band center, consequently governing hydrogen adsorption/desorption energy and reducing the water dissociation barrier—two decisive steps for the HER. Synthesizing these structure-activity relationships, we propose rational design guidelines for high-performance carbides. Finally, this review discusses the practical prospects and remaining challenges associated with industrial-scale water electrolysis for hydrogen production, and highlights promising future directions for enhancing catalyst efficiency.

Next-generation electrical machine insulation systems: Materials, processing technologies, digitalization and circular-sustainability approaches – A critical review
abstract: The electrical insulation system (EIS) is central to the reliability, efficiency, and service lifetime of electrical machines (EMs), yet it remains among the least sustainable elements of EM manufacturing. This review presents a hierarchical analysis of the EIS, spanning primary (enameled conductor coatings), secondary insulation (slot liners and electrical steel coatings), and tertiary insulation systems (impregnation and potting). Each layer is examined in terms of material composition, wet-process technologies, and processing parameters and their effects on dielectric, mechanical, and thermal performance. Advances in material formulations, impregnation and potting methods, and process automation have improved reliability and manufacturing scalability, though often at the cost of higher energy consumption and environmental impact. Identifying failure mechanisms and condition-monitoring strategies contextualizes material and process choices under real operating stresses. The review then identifies emerging pathways toward sustainable insulation, including dry insulation architectures, recyclable and low volatile-organic-compound (VoC) resins, and additive manufacturing for advanced insulation deposition. Integrating life-cycle assessment, eco-design and circular-economy principles is emphasized as essential for sustainable material selection, process design, and end-of-life management. Ultimately this review positions sustainability as a core design variable, equally as important as thermal class and dielectric strength, and a critical step toward next-generation, resource-efficient EMs.

title: The future of supply chain management in Industry 5.0: Emerging challenges and strategic opportunities
abstract: Supply Chain Management (SCM) plays a critical role in integrating suppliers, manufacturers, transporters, and customers to ensure the efficient delivery of products and services. However, traditional supply chains often suffer from limitations, including overstocking, delivery delays, and a lack of real-time visibility. With the emergence of Industry 5.0, there is a growing need for resilient, sustainable, and human-centric SCM systems. This study aims to provide a comprehensive review of the evolution of SCM within the Industry 5.0 paradigm by examining key enabling technologies, architectures, and application scenarios. A structured literature review approach is adopted, focusing on recent contributions in the domain of intelligent supply chains, including technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), blockchain, and edge computing. The analysis highlights that Industry 5.0-driven SCM enhances operational efficiency through real-time data visibility, predictive analytics, and improved coordination across supply chain entities. Furthermore, architectural frameworks and use-case scenarios demonstrate how intelligent supply chains can support cost optimization, agile decision-making, and improved service delivery. The study also identifies critical challenges, including interoperability, data security, infrastructure limitations, and workforce transformation, and outlines future research directions to address these issues.

A critical review of cryogenic hydrogen storage and fuel-system integration for aviation
abstract: Airworthiness qualification of new materials, manufacturing processes and cryogenic system architectures can require 5–9 years after conception, meaning that the generation of certification evidence, rather than material performance, can become the rate-limiting step in translating innovations into aircraft. Liquid hydrogen (LH 2 ) is attractive for medium- and long-range aviation because of its high specific energy, approximately 120 MJ kg −1 , however hydrogen aircraft cannot be realised through fuel substitution alone. This review examines cryogenic hydrogen storage and fuel-system integration for aviation, arguing that LH 2 tanks should be treated as active cryogenic supply systems embedded within the aircraft. It synthesises thermodynamic, fluid, material, structural, safety and certification challenges, drawing on aerospace, maritime and industrial cryogenic systems. A central finding is that desirable design directions are often antagonistic. A heat leak of only 1 W corresponds to approximately 2.24 mg s −1 of hydrogen boil-off, yet reducing heat ingress through more advanced insulation can increase mass and system complexity. Similarly, excess ullage improves pressure-control margin but reduces useable liquid volume, and sloshing controls may introduce thermal bridges. The review reframes aviation LH 2 design as a coupled problem requiring aircraft-scale transient validation, full-field diagnostics, standardised testing and frameworks that capture reliability, inspection and interacting failure modes.

title: Biocrude production via hydrothermal liquefaction of biomass: Recent advances and trends
abstract: Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) appears as a promising way to convert biomass into biocrude, which, in turn, can be upgraded to advanced transportation biofuels. In the last ten years, research on HTL has significantly increased. The necessity for sustainable fuel alternatives originated from the updated EU RED III targets has triggered this growth. This review aims to present the recent progress in HTL by focusing on feedstock diversity, solvent selection, reaction mechanism, and process optimization. A plethora of biomass types has been studied so far, including lignocellulosic residues, municipal and industrial waste, sewage sludge, animal manure, microalgae, and oleaginous yeasts. This fact highlights HTL compatibility and its significant impact towards circular bioeconomy. Furthermore, the major biomass components (cellulose, hemicellulose, lignin, lipids, and proteins) are examined comparatively, along with how water, organic solvents, and co-solvent reaction mediums can impact product distribution and fuel quality. Also, important operational factors like temperature, residence time, reactor loading, pressure, and heating rate are examined concerning biocrude yield and quality. Subsequently, the review dives into studies engaged with extractant selection, catalyst development, aqueous phase recirculation, and the valorization of HTL byproducts. Finally, a summary of recent advances in upgrading methods, scaling up technology, economic analysis, and life cycle assessment is presented to evaluate HTL commercial readiness and sustainability. Overall, this review aims to collectively present all the recent active HTL studies and stress the next steps towards process escalation.

title: “Adoption pathways for green hydrogen in developing economies: A review- driven hybrid modelling framework with policy insights from India”
Identification of technical design constraints and considerations for transmission grid expansion planning projects
abstract: The large-scale deployment of renewable energy sources, particularly offshore wind, requires large-scale transmission grid expansion projects to transmit the produced low-carbon power to the main demand centers. However, the planning and design of such complex projects currently lack a transparent and systematic process that system operators can follow when considering such investments in their grids. This paper identifies and classifies the main technical design constraints and considerations relevant to the planning of transmission grid expansion projects, and more specifically, electrical energy hubs. Seven key areas of interest are identified, namely network integration, HVDC technologies, costs (CAPEX, OPEX, and space requirements), electricity market design, future proofness and modular expandability, reliability-availability-maintainability, and sustainability. Each area of interest is analyzed in terms of its technical and operational relevance, with technical design constraints and considerations derived from such analysis. In addition, a hierarchical classification of the identified constraints and considerations (and therefore areas of interest) is introduced, distinguishing them between three criticality classes, namely hard constraints, main drivers, and key considerations. The dependencies between the different areas are discussed, too. Therefore, this work provides system operators and policymakers with a structured basis to support a transparent planning methodology with clear decision hierarchies for investments in transmission grid expansion projects.

Mitigating wildlife collisions with wind turbines: A review of techniques, evidence, knowledge gaps and avenues for future research
abstract: As global wind energy production rapidly expands, so too have concerns about collision impacts for bird and bat species conservation, driving development of a diversity of anticollision technology. This review compares seven metrics across bat and bird anticollision strategies: (1) detection range, (2) detection probability, (3) species specificity, (4) changes to avoidance behaviour, (5) collision fatalities, (6) setup and maintenance costs, and (7) energy production losses. Of 52 operational and deterrent strategies or tools reviewed, less than half have independent testing data available and many knowledge gaps persist, especially for newer or under-development methods. For large birds, radar systems have greatest detection range (6.13 ± 3.99 km), but limited species specificity, and have no available data for anticollision success. Cameras have shorter range (0.69 ± 0.44 km) but good identification accuracy for large birds (83 ± 20%), with 66 ± 23% collision reduction. Blade painting has had mixed results (two successful and two unsuccessful studies to date; average 7 ± 61% reduction in bird mortalities). For bats, acoustic detection reveals the most proximal collision risk, and acoustic-activated curtailment shows the greatest success in reducing fatalitites (66 ± 34% anticollision success), while ultrasonic bat deterrents have had limited success (23 ± 40% reduction in fatalities). Technology investment ranges from relatively low (e.g., blade feathering below cut-in, blanket curtailment, deterrents such as vegetation removal through mowing, or blade painting prior to construction), through to very high (e.g., radar, camera, and acoustic detection systems for smart curtailment), with varying degrees of maintenance also required. There is a general lack of data on the lost revenue due to energy production losses. Additional data on energy production losses are required to balance the economic costs of curtailment with conservation benefits (i.e. fatalities per MWh) to help inform decisions in selecting mitigation approaches for the wind industry. This review provides researchers, project proponents, and policy makers with a scientific and comprehensive reference for the effectivness of anticollision technology, improving biodiversity outcomes for this important renewable energy resource.
